rule: A liability cap must be present. Absence of any cap is unacceptable.
rationale: Uncapped liability exposes the client to unbounded damages from a single dispute.

rule: Indemnification should be mutual, not one-sided in favor of the counterparty.
rationale: One-sided indemnification shifts all risk of third-party claims onto the client regardless of fault.

rule: The cancellation notice window must be at least 30 days. Notice windows shorter than 30 days, or windows longer than 120 days, should be flagged.
rationale: Sub-30-day windows are easy to miss operationally; 120+ day windows lock the client in far earlier than typical renewal planning cycles.

rule: Confidentiality obligations should not survive termination for more than 5 years (60 months) unless the subject matter is trade secrets.
rationale: Indefinite or excessively long confidentiality tails create open-ended compliance risk.

rule: The client should have a termination-for-convenience right or, at minimum, a termination-for-breach right with a reasonable cure period.
rationale: Without either, the client is locked into the full term regardless of the counterparty's performance.
